reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator of normative psychology is the causal mapping S → R mediated by M. This structure implies a conditional probability distribution P(R|S,M), where M acts as a latent variable. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian inference over M’s posterior distribution given S and R data. The derivation begins with empirical observation of S-R pairs, followed by hypothesis generation of M as an intervening variable. The dual nature of M—both antecedent (M_ant) and consequent (M_con)—suggests a layered causal architecture. In GSE, this becomes a state-transition model where M evolves through discrete steps, capturing dynamic aspects of cognition. Failure modes arise when M is under-specified or when S-R correlations exceed normative expectations. The mathematical framework supports both static inference and dynamic simulation, enabling robust modeling of human-like behavior under controlled conditions.
